messages:
incident-bot: Paging SREs — p99 latency spike detected for /v1/generate-stream in region us-west2. Alert threshold breached at 07:12 UTC. Affected: streaming sessions with live tokens; p95 -> 720ms (norm 110ms), p99 -> 2.9s (norm 280ms). Error rate stable. Link: https://ops.redwood/incoming/alerts/1749991234
Alex M: acked. oncall? looks like streaming stalls not full errors, connections held open longer.
Katelyn S: I’m oncall, taking this. joining bridge: +1. Checking routing tables and LB health now.
Jamal R: seeing spike in router hop times in /metrics: router.router_latency.p99{region="us-west2"} jump coincident with a routing-policy rollout at 2024-11-30T02:00Z. Policy name: prefer-local-v2.
Priya D: fwiw we rolled prefer-local-v2 to 10% last night, but rollout job shows a seed change in balancer mapping around that time. Could be a hash remap creating a hotfanout.
Katelyn S: timeline: p99 started ~07:12 UTC, prefer-local-v2 rollout step at 02:00 UTC — no obvious immediate correlation but might be slow heat-up. pulling LB assignments for the last hour.
ops-bot: Query: lb.assignments.top_shards(1h) -> shard-13: 47% of active streams, next shard 6%
Alex M: hot-shard confirmed. shard-13 is owning nearly half of traffic for stream route. that explains tail latencies due to queuing on a few backends.
Jamal R: also seeing cross-zone fanout from shard-13: 72% of traffic routed from us-west2 to eu-west1 replicas (region skew). Likely a routing policy fallback sending to remote replicas when local servers report soft overload.
Katelyn S: customers impacted? support dashboard?
Support Bot: Support query spike: +18 incoming tickets referencing "stream lag" and "partial responses" in us-west2. Current estimated affected customers: ~2.7% of active orgs with streaming enabled.
Priya D: quick mitigation options: 1) throttle fanout by reducing cross-region fallback weight, 2) temporarily roll back prefer-local-v2 to previous mapping, 3) apply manual hotkey split (evict or shard-split) for shard-13, 4) scale up dedicated pool in us-west2.
Alex M: prefer-local-v2 rollback is low-risk and fast. patch to revert to prefer-local-v1. If rolling back, we need to monitor p95/p99 for 10m rolling window.
Katelyn S: agree. I’ll run rollback to 0% for prefer-local-v2 and drain new assignments. Patching via infra-config: 
```
# rollback prefer-local-v2
curl -X POST https://infra-api/configs/rollouts/revert \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"policy":"prefer-local-v2","target":0}'
```
Katelyn S: starting rollback now.
ops-bot: rollout revert job queued (job id: r-2024-11-30-rollback-174999). Estimated 45s to propagate to edge controllers.
Jamal R: while rollback propagates, we should also limit cross-region fallback weight to avoid eu-west1 extra hop. patching loadbalancer weight: set fallback_weight_usw2->0.2 (was 0.6).
Alex M: do that after rollback starts. please post the exact command.
Katelyn S: running weight patch: 
```
kubectl -n infra exec lb-configger -- curl -X PATCH \
  http://localhost:8080/config -d '{"fallback_weight":0.2}'
```
Katelyn S: applied. verify logs.
ops-bot: lb-config change accepted (confirm id: cfg-174999-1).
Priya D: getting a snapshot of shard assignments now.
ops-bot: lb.assignments.top_shards(5m) -> shard-13: 22% (was 47%), shard-9: 11%, shard-12: 9%
Alex M: nice, shard concentration reduced. monitoring p99.
Katelyn S: p95 trending down: 430ms -> 180ms within 90s of rollback, p99: 2.9s -> 980ms and falling. still some streaming stalls.
Jamal R: investigate backend queue length on nodes serving shard-13.
ops-bot: query: backend.queue.length{shard="shard-13"} -> node-a: 42, node-b: 47, node-c: 3. Looks like two overloaded replicas, one healthy.
Priya D: why are two replicas overloaded? Are they pinned to a certain GPU instance type due to capacity scheduling?
Alex M: yep, deployment constraints pinned those replicas to older VMs (no autoscale). we can evict and let autoscaler refill if needed.
Katelyn S: plan: 1) continue rollback and monitor 2) cycle the two overloaded replicas (cordon + drain) 3) if stalls persist, temporarily route shard-13 to more replicas (manual split).
Katelyn S: cordon+drain node-a and node-b for shard-13 now.
ops-bot: cordon/drain jobs started. expected 90s per node to reschedule.
Support Bot: update to support: we’ve mitigated a major routing imbalance; customers may see transient improvements. Recommend holding public comms until we confirm sustained p99 < 500ms for 15 minutes.
Jamal R: after draining, queue lengths: node-a: 6, node-b: 8, node-c: 2. good.
Alex M: streaming stalls dropped from ~9.8% to 1.1% of sessions in us-west2. p99 currently 460ms.
Katelyn S: continuing to watch. Will keep rollout at 0% for prefer-local-v2 and mark the policy rollout blocked. Opening a postmortem ticket to follow up on mapping entropy and rollout control.
Priya D: filing ticket now: PM-174999 - "prefer-local-v2 rollout caused hotfanout due to seed remap -> hot-shard". I'll include heap of logs and the LB snapshot.
Katelyn S: oncall handoff in 25m to duty rotation. leaving runbook notes: rollback applied, fallback weight lowered, nodes drained and rescheduled. still open: investigate why rollout mapping caused shard-13 to absorb disproportionate streams (seed choice + sticky hashing).
Alex M: customers to contact: 1 large media customer in us-west2 reported rebuffering on live stream — flagged as Sev3. Priya can coordinate comms with support.
Priya D: will draft a short note: what happened, what we did (policy rollback + LB weight change + node drain), and next steps (postmortem + fix to rollout job to avoid seed remap).
Katelyn S: thanks team. leaving bridge, handing to next oncall @Jamal R in 25m. if p99 creeps back, alert ops.
Jamal R: ack; I’ll take bridge after handoff. saving logs and commands in the incident channel.
incident-bot: Incident update: mitigated -> monitoring. Please update incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood/1749991234
Katelyn S: final snapshot before handoff: p95 120ms, p99 410ms, streaming stalls 0.9% (baseline 0.6%). marking as under observation.
Jamal R: oncall notes added. postmortem ticket created and assigned to Priya and Alex.
Support Bot: support queue update: ticket surge reduced to normal levels.
Alex M: follow-up actions (assigned): - investigate hash seed selection (Alex) - add rollout chaos guard to detect hotfanout (Priya) - improve LB fallback telemetry to show cross-region fanout (Katelyn).
Priya D: I’ll start the rollout guard design doc and post to eng-ml for review.
Katelyn S: handing off. bridge closed for now. thanks all :thumbsup:
